content: In section 3.7 of the Mafāḥiṣ Ibn Turka says the spoken form of the letters pertains to prophethood, given its mission to benefit the masses, while the mental and written forms are peculiar to walāya: the mental to the elite of that category, the written to the Seal of Sainthood (presumably ʿAlī, in Melvin-Koushki's gloss), his family and his heirs. He shows this from the fact that the Prophet dwelt almost exclusively on the spoken form.
